task: Locate the first beat of a four-beat bar within an existing regular beat grid; not tempo estimation or within-beat onset repair.
data: Existing annotated recordings in the original component-isolated train/validation/test partitions. No new downloads, consumed fresh timing inputs or independent timing model scores.
scope: A supporting alignment/loop experiment; not evidence of song-pair compatibility or perceptual mix quality.
label_integrity: Every beat must match a unique consecutive manual beat and the complete 1-2-3-4 sequence; reject missing/extra beats and irregular windows.
features: Beat-scale raw acoustic contexts, excluding all time/position/BPM fields. Seventy-six per-beat descriptors, local median/IQR normalization, four phase pools of means and standard deviations; rotate pools around each proposed downbeat.
invariance: No absolute candidate-index input. One shared scorer evaluates all four rotations; rolling the input must roll the scores.
weighting: Each track has equal total mass; candidate weights are renormalized to the candidate count. Each window has four candidates, exactly one positive.
calibration: Choose tree size and temperature by validation track-weighted multiclass log loss only. Then select a correction threshold on validation.
validation_gate: At least 10% coverage of synthetic wrong bar claims; at least 90% corrected-claim precision; at most 5% false changes when the supplied claim is already correct; positive improvement over the real automatic-grid phase-zero baseline.
test_gate: Same criteria on held-out phase-model source IDs, plus positive lower bound of track-bootstrap 95% natural-grid improvement. No test tuning.
deployment: No live library grid writes. Do not enable even preview correction unless the fixed offline gate passes; musical listening validation remains separate.
limitations: Source partitions were used by earlier timing/structure experiments; this is a new-task held-out benchmark, not an untouched overall project confirmation.
A pre-fit metadata audit inspected split sizes and phase counts, not any phase-model predictions.
Only clean one-to-one automatic/manual beat correspondences are evaluated; inference needs the same grid-regularity guard.
Four-beat meter assumed. EDM corpus transfer to other styles remains unproven.
